meta.title: Disable unused Kubernetes service-account token automount
meta.author: Codex manager

feature.problem_statement: The application Deployment uses a Kubernetes ServiceAccount without disabling automatic token projection, although the server has no Kubernetes API integration and does not need an in-cluster credential.
goals: Disable service-account token automount at the application pod boundary.
Assert the hardening in CI and DEV Helm contract renders.
Preserve migration-hook, Vault TokenRequest, startup, and probe behavior.
non_goals: Adding Kubernetes API access, RBAC, or a compatibility fallback.
Changing the migration Job token contract or Vault SecretStore authentication.
scope_in: Application Deployment pod spec and optionally chart-created ServiceAccount hardening.
Helm contract tests and negative missing/true fixtures.

requirements.statement: The application Deployment pod spec must render automountServiceAccountToken: false for both CI/external-database and DEV/CNPG values.
requirements.rationale: Pod-level enforcement also protects deployments that use an externally managed ServiceAccount.

requirements.statement: Helm contract validation must reject a missing or true application automount setting and cover both rendered environments.
requirements.rationale: A future chart edit must not silently reintroduce an unnecessary credential.

requirements.statement: When the chart creates the application ServiceAccount, it should also render automountServiceAccountToken: false as defense in depth.
requirements.rationale: The generated identity should be safe independently of pod-template enforcement.

requirements.statement: Deployment documentation must state that future Kubernetes API access requires explicit opt-in and narrow RBAC.
requirements.rationale: The security boundary and future exception path must remain discoverable.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given CI and DEV Helm values, when the chart is rendered, then the application pod spec contains boolean automountServiceAccountToken false.
Given a rendered Deployment with the field missing or true, when Helm contract validation runs, then validation fails.
Given chart-created ServiceAccount values, when the chart is rendered, then its automount setting is false.
Given the deployment runbook, when an operator considers Kubernetes API access, then the explicit opt-in and narrow-RBAC rule is documented.

test_plan.approach: Render CI and DEV values, assert Deployment and created ServiceAccount fields, and exercise missing/true negative fixtures.
Run Helm lint, strict schema/render checks, existing helmcontract tests, Go tests, and Python checker tests.
After merge, verify explicit DEV Argo/Deployment readiness, migration completion, health/readiness, and Vault SecretStore/ExternalSecret readiness.

review_checks: Pod-level false is present in both environments

perspectives.summary: Keep the change pod-scoped, chart-contract tested, and limited to an unused credential.
Require false boolean in rendered Deployment and generated ServiceAccount, with negative fixtures.
Preserve Vault TokenRequest and migration-hook behavior and verify explicit DEV readiness.

council.consensus_summary: Implement a fail-closed Helm hardening change with pod-level enforcement, defense-in-depth ServiceAccount metadata, contract negatives, and explicit DEV rollout checks.
